ground_truth.unit: log points of annualised household electricity consumption (kWh)
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("Effect of the Reform on Residential Electricity Consumption and Expenditure (2011-2014)"), column (1), row Reform (T): the paper's difference-in-differences estimate of the August 2013 Spanish electricity pricing reform (fixed charge raised, regulated volumetric rate cut) on household electricity consumption, estimated by OLS.  Data: Spanish Household Budget Survey households interviewed between August 2011 and April 2014, each interviewed twice, in the same two-week period of two consecutive years; the control group has both interviews before the reform, the treated group its second interview after it.  T is the post-reform dummy for interviews whose electricity bill falls under the reform (the paper places the response one month after the reform, when households receive a reformed bill).  Dependent variable: log of electricity consumption in the month before the interview (kWh, annualised by the survey).  Regressors: T, log household price per kWh (expenditure divided by consumption), log income and its square, months since reform, and controls for household size, number of rooms, dwelling surface, elderly members, education of the household head, household economic situation (number of economically active members), renting, building older than 25 years, municipality-size dummies, urban area, province capital, regional dummies, quarterly dummies and year fixed effects.  No household fixed effects.  Standard errors clustered at the household level.

i4r.notes: Team 49 blanket verdict (code reproduces the paper's output); no meta-database row for column 1.

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=-0.113062 vs claimed=-0.178 (relative error 36.48%, tolerance 15.17%, the ±1·SE band with SE=0.027).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Common estimation sample for all eight columns = the 25,775-row 2011-2014 panel (rows with non-missing T2) restricted to complete cases on all regression variables including the three instruments (household effective prices of potatoes, water and fuel, lnp_papas/lnp_aguav/lnp_gascar, which exist only when the household bought the good): 10,295 obs, 7,000 households. Singleton households (3,705) are kept in the sample count and household count; they do not affect within estimates (fixest drops them internally). Without singletons the FE sample would be 6,590 obs / 3,295 households.
LIML implemented by hand as a k-class estimator (fixest has no LIML); household FE models are estimated by within-demeaning all variables first. SEs clustered by household.

Controls: ln income and its square (lny, lny2 as supplied), months since reform (dist), household size, rooms, m2, elderly dummy, education (4 levels), economic situation (3 levels, SITUACTHOG_j), renting, building >25 yrs, urban, province capital, municipality-size dummies, region (CCAA) dummies, quarter dummies, year FE. Retirement-income dummy not included (not in the paper's control list).

Because the household price is defined as expenditure/consumption, ln(expenditure) = ln(consumption) + ln(price) identically in the data; with ln(price) on the right-hand side the expenditure regressions therefore give exactly the same Reform coefficient as the consumption regressions (price coefficient shifted by +1) under OLS, FE and LIML (LIML is invariant to this reparameterisation). Reported as computed; not adjusted.
Instruments are weak in this sample (first-stage F about 6 without FE, about 3 with FE).
cell.notes: Data: analysis CSV 'Data_to run_DOFILE3.csv' (prepared variables used: lnc_ele, lng_ele, lnp_kwh, lnp_* instruments, T2 = post-reform interview dummy, Tm = treated group, dist = months since reform). Table 1 means on the T2 sample (25,775 obs: consumption 3,425 kWh, expenditure 754 EUR, T mean 0.19) confirmed the panel definition. Readme.pdf was not opened. attempt-1 and attempt-2 are exploratory runs (no RESULT lines). Process note: one sandbox invocation was launched by mistake before attempt-2's script.R existed (Docker mounted an empty directory in its place; it ran ~1 s with no output); its empty outputs were deleted and attempt-2 was then run properly with the script in place. No run hung.
